title: Composition basics
examples: How can I make a simple tune sound more complex?
What is the difference between a motif and a theme?
Can you give me an example of musical development?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how music is built.
A motif is a very short musical idea you repeat.
For example, think of a simple three-note pattern.
Structure refers to the overall plan of the music piece.
Development is when you change or expand that original motif.
In real life, music structure is like a story you tell.

faq.q: What is the difference between a motif and a theme?
faq.a: A motif is usually very short, like just a few notes. A theme is a longer, more complete musical idea.
asks: Are motifs and themes the same thing?
Can I use a motif to build a theme?

faq.q: How do I know when I need to develop a motif?
faq.a: You develop it when the music needs more interest or energy. You can make it sound bigger or change its mood.
asks: When should I change my motif?

faq.q: Is structure just about repeating sections?
faq.a: No, structure is the whole plan. It shows how the different sections relate to each other in order.
asks: What is the overall plan of a song?

faq.q: Can I develop a motif using only rhythm?
faq.a: Yes, you can change the rhythm by making the notes faster or slower. This is a common development technique.

faq.q: If I change the key, is that development?
faq.a: Yes, changing the key or harmony is a way to develop the motif. It gives the listener a new colour.
asks: Does changing keys count as development?

facts: A motif is a very short, recurring musical idea.
Structure refers to the overall organization of a piece of music.
Development involves altering existing musical material.
Techniques for development include changing rhythm, harmony, or tempo.

quiz.say: A piece of music that keeps repeating the exact same four-note pattern over and over is primarily focusing on:
quiz.why: The definition of a motif is a short, memorable musical idea that is repeated.

wrong.1: Structure is the overall plan, not just one small idea.
wrong.2: Development requires changing the motif, not just repeating it.
wrong.3: Harmony refers to chords played together, not the short repeating idea itself.

quiz.say: If a composer takes a simple melody and plays it first in a major key, then in a minor key, they are demonstrating:
quiz.show: Changing the mood of the music
quiz.why: Changing the key or harmony is a way of developing the original musical material.

wrong.0: A motif is the original short idea, not the act of changing it.
wrong.1: Structure is the arrangement of sections, not the transformation of one idea.
wrong.2: Tempo only refers to the speed, not the emotional key change.

quiz.say: Which term describes the overall plan, like Introduction, Verse, Chorus, Bridge,?
quiz.why: Structure describes the large-scale organization of the entire piece.

wrong.0: Harmony is about the chords, not the sequence of sections.
wrong.2: A motif is too small; it is just a small musical building block.
wrong.3: Development is an action applied to the motif, not the plan itself.
